choices.assertion: Metadata rows show each filename, format, byte size and named remove button. Removing the middle row preserves neighboring files and form values; file-content and outbound-access traps stayed at zero.
choices.remaining: Long filename is retained and CSS permits wrapping; line breaks at physical browser widths were not measured.

choices.assertion: Names, formats (including MIME and unknown fallback), localized byte sizes and count appear after selecting files. Synthetic cancel and empty change retain the selection; byte reads, fetch, XHR and beacon traps stayed at zero.
choices.remaining: A native OS picker or physical assistive technology was not used, and the visual presentation of very long filenames has not been measured.

choices.assertion: Replacement help is associated with the chooser; replacing two selected files with one replaces the complete list; cancel preserves existing rows, and name, phone and email are retained.

Middle removal gives focus to the following named button; after final removal focus returns to the chooser. A persistent polite, atomic status identifies the removed filename. Counts, remaining rows and other fields are checked.

Count above three, individual size above 5,000,000 bytes and unsupported format each expose the expected localized reason on selection. Removal clears the error; submission at the exact limit produces one local receipt. With up to three permitted files, a separate total above 15,000,000 bytes necessarily violates an earlier rule.
All four workforce service CTAs open F01 with the matching service. The form identifies its four required fields and creates a local receipt; the receipt opens the exact sample in ADMIN.

All three programs enter both form modes with their slug preselected. F05 has no attachment field and F06 accepts empty email/files. Each synthetic record retains its program, type and source, and its receipt opens the matching ADMIN detail.

Jobs, Careers and Saved Jobs each preserved the other filter, confirmed exact before/after record IDs and counts, and focused the following chip then the initial search field. The tested chip labels identify the removed criterion.
